Combines classical epistemology (JTB, Gettier, reliabilism, Pollock & Cruz's procedural/defeater theory) with a Sri Vidya source text (Smriti/Shruti, Vijnanamaya Kosha, 'knowledge is one but understood in ten ways') to reject 'knowledge = true information' and propose knowledge as a multi-dimensional, quantifiable, non-scalar construct: a Knowledge Vector K=(Truth,Justification,Reliability,Anti-luck,Stability-under-defeaters,Competence,Uncertainty); formalizes reliability R(f)=P(true output|f), counterfactual robustness CR(p), defeater resistance DR(p) (rebutting vs undercutting defeaters), competence via held-out task performance, and an information-gain uncertainty measure with an explicit warning that entropy/mutual information are not automatically epistemic-knowledge measures; proposes a composite scalar K* explicitly as a decision-oriented projection of the canonical vector, never a replacement for it; introduces a 'KNOWLEDGE CLAIM' epistemic-object ontology (proposition+evidence+provenance+justification+inference-path+reliability+defeaters+counterfactual-tests+temporal-validity+competence-evidence+uncertainty) replacing a flat document/fact/embedding ontology; derives Knowledge Invariance KI (agreement across independent representations), and amount-of-knowledge quantities (Coverage KC, Reliability KR, Depth, Robustness KB, Transfer KT) rendered as a 'Knowledge Profile' report card rather than one scalar; states knowledge decay (K(p,t1)!=K(p,t2)) and time-indexing; validates (per the source's own claim) the existing observation-vs-knowledge-claim architectural distinction; ties into the batch's Dhatu hypothesis by reframing knowledge acquisition as a transformation pipeline rather than a static object; closes by recommending a formal 15-part 'Knowledge Ontology & Measurement Framework v1.0' deliverable mapping to Zero/Dhatu and to KnowledgeOS.

aliases: knowledge as a temporal state machine / trajectory
note: Sharpens 'knowledge is a continuously changing body of facts' into a temporal model: a fact is not 'X is true' but a tuple F=(claim,evidence,context,time,source,validity); Knowledge(t) is a state of accumulated/structured facts, so Knowledge(t1)!=Knowledge(t2) as facts appear/are confirmed/contradicted/become obsolete/relationships and confidence change; distinguishes Knowledge from Truth via an architecture-migration example (Valid(F,t1)=true, Valid(F,t2)=false or Status(F,t2)=historical), arguing KnowledgeOS must preserve trajectory/history rather than delete superseded facts; generalizes to K(t)=f(O_<=t,E_<=t,C_<=t) (observations, evidence, contextual interpretation up to t); extends an existing Davidson-invariance idea by distinguishing what changes (representation/language/measurement/interpretation/model) from what remains invariant (relationships/truth conditions/structural properties), yielding Knowledge = Temporal Fact State + Relations + Evidence + Invariants; issues a correction that Fact != Knowledge (an unobserved true event is a fact but not knowledge for anyone), redefining Knowledge = Facts/claims + Evidence + Justification + Context + Temporal validity + Relationships = K(t); reframes the guiding question from 'how much knowledge does a system contain' to 'what is the current state of its continuously evolving body of justified facts, and how did that state change over time', proposing knowledge as a temporal state machine/trajectory rather than a static repository.
